subject: Post-call follow-up: CardioSense data handling & retention options
messages:
From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@cardiosense.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling questions from today's call

Hi Neha —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. A few items came up on our side that we need clarified before we take this to Legal/Procurement: 

1) PII / user content retention — CardioSense needs a firm guarantee that patient-identifiable data (names, MRNs, SSNs, free-text clinical notes) will not be retained beyond the inference request unless explicitly stored by us. Is a 0-retention profile available that ensures request/response bodies are not persisted?

2) Logs and observability — we understand you keep some operational logs for reliability. Can you confirm the shortest possible retention window for debug/trace logs and for per-request metadata (IP, timestamp, model id)? Our threshold for production is 7 days or less for anything that could be tied back to a patient.

3) Data residency / KMS — we require EU-only processing (eu-west-1) and customer-managed keys for any keys used to encrypt request payloads or caches. Is that supported for a Private/Dedicated setup?

4) Evidence — can you provide a sample DPA addendum and SOC 2 + ISO attestations we can share with Legal?

If you can send a brief recap and proposed configuration options we’ll share with Legal and procurement. We’re targeting an initial pilot (10k tokens/month) in September if this aligns. 

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform Integrations, CardioSense
alex.thompson@cardiosense.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@cardiosense.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling questions from today's call

Alex — great questions, appreciate the clarity. Quick post-call recap and concrete options below. I’ve attached a short PDF that maps our standard profiles and a starter DPA addendum for you and Legal to review (redwood-data-retention-options.pdf).

Summary (high-level):
- 0-retention profile (recommended for high-PII workloads): request and response bodies are not written to persistent storage. KV caches can be configured to 0 days. We surface only aggregate metrics.
- Short-log window profile: retains operational traces and per-request metadata for debugging/observability. Options: 72-hour (default low-level debug), 7-day (short window for auditability), 30-day (standard). All logs can be filtered to remove free-text payloads.
- EU-only deployment: we support private/dedicated deployments in eu-west-1 with customer KMS (BYOK) and VPC peering.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report and ISO artifacts available for NDA; sample DPA addendum attached for markups.

Tradeoffs and recommended next steps:
- 0-retention for user content reduces available telemetry for debugging. For the pilot, we recommend 0-retention for request/response bodies + a 7-day short-log window for per-request metadata (IP, timestamps, model id) with redaction of free-text fields. That gives a workable balance for triage while meeting tight privacy requirements.
- If CardioSense requires absolute 0 logs (including audit metadata), we’ll need to scope a custom dedicated deployment with acceptance of limited observability and extended onboarding to validate SLOs.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (options + config matrix)

Suggested next steps:
1) Legal/Procurement review the attached DPA addendum and flag changes.
2) Karthik can provide technical ops note on implementation constraints (I’ve cc’d him).
3) If we get alignment, I’ll spin up a eu-west-1 pilot with the 0-body/7-day-metadata profile and share a test plan and timeline (target: pilot kickoff in early Sept).

Do you want a short call with Legal and Karthik this week to walk the DPA?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@cardiosense.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Data handling questions from today's call

Alex / Neha — adding detail on what’s feasible from the infra/security side. Attaching a short ops note (security-ops-note.txt).

Key technical constraints and options:
- Request/response bodies (full text): we can run a "no-persistent-logs" profile on Dedicated or Private that prevents bodies from being written to persistent disk. In that mode we still keep ephemeral in-memory KV cache for inference; KV can be set to 0-day eviction at the application layer.
- Traces & debug artifacts: internal tracing and kernel-level logs are generated during inference. For production-grade runs we can rotate and purge these automatically. Minimum practical retention for those low-level artifacts is 72 hours to allow crash triage and hotfixes.
- Per-request metadata (model id, route, IP hashes, timestamps): by default we keep limited metadata for 30 days. We can contractually limit this to 7 days for the pilot and apply IP hashing + salt to reduce re-identification risk.
- Redaction pipeline: we offer an optional pre-ingest redaction module to strip predictable PII patterns (SSN, MRN, names) before tokenization. Customers can also call our client-side redaction library.
- KMS & region: eu-west-1 + BYOK supported on a Private deployment. KMS-managed keys used for ephemeral volumes and persisted artifacts in scope of the DPA only.

Caveats:
- Absolute zero-logs (no metadata) will remove some observability required to hit latency/availability SLOs — we can do it, but SLA will need to be adjusted and we’ll require an extended validation period.

Attachments: security-ops-note.txt

If you like, I can produce a short appendix enumerating the exact log categories and the retention windows we propose for the pilot (72h traces, 7d metadata, 0d bodies).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Applied Security, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@cardiosense.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: CardioSense Legal <legal@cardiosense.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 10:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling questions from today's call

Thanks Neha / Karthik — helpful detail. CardioSense is comfortable moving forward with the pilot under the following configuration: 

- Request/response bodies: 0-retention (no persistent storage)
- KV cache evicted immediately (0 days)
- Per-request metadata: 7-day retention
- Traces/kernel artifacts: 72-hour retention
- EU-only processing (eu-west-1) with BYOK
- Redaction enabled (we will use client-side redaction for PHI where possible)

Please share the DPA addendum and SOC 2 documents with our Legal contact. Procurement note: we’ll need a DocuSign-ready addendum and a PO note within two weeks to hit an early-September pilot start.

Alex
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform Integrations, CardioSense
